output.subject: We've received your concerns about your mother's account
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for contacting us about your mother's account. We can hear how worrying this is, and we're sorry for the distress it has caused you and your family.

We want to confirm that we have received your complaint. You told us that your mother has dementia, and that her aide has been cashing checks made out to herself. You mentioned this amounts to nine checks totalling about $7,340 since May. You also told us that your mother could not have signed these checks, and you asked us what you should do.

A specialist team is now reviewing what you have shared and will respond to you within 10 business days. We understand you are looking for guidance on next steps, and the team's response will address your question.

In the meantime, if there are any further details you would like to share, you are welcome to reply to this message.

Kind regards,

Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: Suspected elder financial abuse with possibly ongoing losses; decide whether contact or protective action is needed sooner than the 10-business-day window.
The writer is a family member, not the account holder; confirm their authority (e.g., power of attorney) before discussing account details.
Customer asked what to do; decide what guidance to give (e.g., stopping further checks, police report) and add it before sending or in the follow-up.
Verify the reported figures (9 checks, about $7,340 since May) against account records.
Reply makes no commitment on reimbursement or fault; keep it that way unless a decision has been made.
Consider whether the aide may have access to the mother's mail or email when choosing how to deliver correspondence.
